# Platform parity table

Every user-facing feature and setting (`manifest.toml`), bindable action (`actions.toml`), navigation layer entry (`layer_actions.toml`) and interactive menu row (`menu_manifest.json`), with its status on each OS. Regenerate with `node tools/codegen/codegen-platform-parity.cjs`; `tools/test/test-linux-feature-parity.cjs` fails when this file is stale or a rule below breaks.

- ✓ **supported**: the catalogue declares it there, and the linked production file is its owner: the file of that driver whose code spells the entry the most often (`+n`: other files that spell it). « (declared) » marks an owner `platform_parity.toml` names because the entry is read generically (a section loop, a slot prefix, a data-driven layer). An owner is source evidence, not proof that the feature works on a real machine.
- ◐ **degraded**: supported, but only on some sessions or hardware of that OS; the reason says which.
- — **unavailable**: the catalogue leaves that OS out. The key is the reason the menu shows, present in all 21 locales; the technical reason and its class are in the reason list below.

The gate checks that every non-supported cell has a reason key present in the 21 locales and a technical reason, that every supported or degraded cell has an owner on that OS (or a recorded PPT-nn finding), and that no menu row bound to a feature shows on an OS where the feature is unavailable.

| `platform_reason.personal_shortcut_switches_are_windows`             | os_concept     | These switches name personal setups of the Windows AutoHotkey shortcuts (broken laptop key remap, window dragging and tab switching with the mouse, programmable keyboard, professional environment) that have no macOS or Linux counterpart.                                                                  | Windows only: these five switches name personal Windows setups (a broken laptop key, window dragging and tab switching with the mouse, a programmable keyboard, a professional environment). macOS and Linux have no counterpart.                                                                                          |    10 |
| `platform_reason.profile_shortcut_uses_prompt_action`                | os_equivalent  | On Windows and Linux a custom profile is bound through the AI prediction with a chosen prompt action, which applies the profile to that request only.                                                                                                                                                          | On Windows and Linux, assign “AI prediction with a chosen prompt” to a keyboard shortcut and choose your custom profile in the action picker. The profile applies to that request only; the action is refused if the profile was deleted or AI is disabled.                                                                |     2 |
| `platform_reason.proxy_override_is_native_settings`                  | driver_storage | macOS and Linux keep the proxy override in the driver's own settings store, not in config.toml.                                                                                                                                                                                                                | On macOS and Linux this setting is kept in the driver's own settings store, not in config.toml.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |     2 |
| `platform_reason.remap_engine_is_per_driver`                         | os_concept     | Windows remaps with its own AutoHotkey tap-hold layer, macOS with Karabiner-Elements (its virtual HID driver, login items and approvals), Linux with the evdev/uinput tap-hold daemon; the setup rows of one engine do not apply to another.                                                                   | Each driver remaps the keyboard with a different engine — Windows with its own tap-hold layer, macOS with Karabiner-Elements, Linux with the tap-hold engine in its own daemon — so each carries the menu for the engine it runs, and none of them can configure another's.                                                |    21 |
| `platform_reason.selection_operations_are_a_block_on_linux`          | menu_layout    | Linux groups CapsWord, case transforms, select word or line and plain paste in one menu block; macOS reaches them through Ctrl shortcuts and Windows through its key combinations.                                                                                                                             | Linux only: this driver groups its selection operations — CapsWord, the case transforms, select word or line, paste without formatting — into one block. macOS reaches the same operations through its Ctrl shortcuts and Windows through its own key combinations, so a shared row would list them twice there.           |    16 |
| `platform_reason.shortcut_settings_are_stored_per_driver`            | driver_storage | Each driver binds actions on the chords its OS leaves free (Win combinations, Ctrl and Cmd, Linux keyboard slots) and stores the choice under a slot id of its own (`meta_*`, `secondary_*`, `primary_*` in shortcuts.keyboard); the same action is assignable on every OS.                                    | This shortcut belongs to the system that binds it: each driver offers its actions on the chords its own system leaves free (Windows key combinations on Windows, Ctrl and Cmd on macOS, keyboard slots on Linux) and stores the choice under its own name.                                                                 |    86 |
| `platform_reason.shortcuts_restore_is_composed_on_macos`             | not_yet        | macOS keeps its key combinations in Karabiner settings, and no restore yet rebuilds them together with the other shortcut settings outside the Configuration menu's restore.                                                                                                                                   | Not on macOS yet: its key combinations are kept in the Karabiner settings, and only the Configuration menu's restore brings them back together with the other shortcut settings.                                                                                                                                           |     2 |
| `platform_reason.token_streaming_unvalidated_on_windows`             | not_yet        | Token-by-token display uses the WinHTTP streaming path, which has not been validated on Windows; the option stays inactive there until it is.                                                                                                                                                                  | Not on Windows yet: the token-by-token display has not been validated on Windows, so this option stays inactive.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |     1 |
| `platform_reason.touchpad_stack_is_per_driver`                       | os_concept     | Each driver reads the touchpad through its own stack (Windows Precision Touchpad settings, Hammerspoon gesture events, Linux evdev and libinput), so the status, setup and slot rows of one stack do not exist on the others.                                                                                  | Each driver reads the touchpad through a different stack — Windows through its precision-touchpad API, macOS through Hammerspoon's gesture events, Linux through evdev — so the slots each can offer, and the setup each needs, are its own.                                                                               |    41 |
| `platform_reason.tray_top_level_rows_are_each_drivers`               | os_concept     | The in-app updater row exists on Linux, the suspend switch on Windows (AutoHotkey Suspend); each tray carries the top-level rows its runtime has.                                                                                                                                                              | Each driver's tray carries the top-level rows its platform has: the in-app updater on Linux, the suspend switch on Windows. The others reach the same ground elsewhere or not at all.                                                                                                                                      |    10 |
| `platform_reason.virtual_keyboard_is_karabiner`                      | os_concept     | The Karabiner-Elements virtual HID keyboard type decides which keycodes the two ISO-only keys reach on macOS; Windows and Linux name these keys by scan code and have no virtual keyboard.                                                                                                                     | macOS only: Karabiner-Elements, which Ergopti uses on macOS to remap keys, has a virtual keyboard whose type decides which keycodes the two ISO-only keys reach. Windows and Linux name these keys by position and have no virtual keyboard.                                                                               |     4 |
| `platform_reason.windows_touchpad_slots_are_three_and_four_fingers`  | os_api         | Windows Precision Touchpad settings expose only three- and four-finger taps and the four straight swipes as assignable gestures, and deliver them to applications as hotkeys; no raw contact data reaches a user-mode application, so two- and five-finger, diagonal and horizontal-axis slots cannot be read. | Not on Windows: Windows Settings lets you assign a shortcut only to three- and four-finger taps and to swipes in the four straight directions, and passes no touch data to Ergopti. There are no two- or five-finger slots, diagonals or horizontal-swipe slots there.                                                     |    83 |
| `platform_reason.wrap_selection_is_a_shortcut_key_on_macos`          | driver_storage | macOS lists the option among its Ctrl and Cmd shortcuts and stores it as shortcuts.keys.wrap_text_if_selected.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Not on macOS under this name: macOS lists this option among its Ctrl and Cmd shortcuts and stores it with them, as shortcuts.keys.wrap_text_if_selected.                                                                                                                                                                   |     2 |
